indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one piece is wrapped round another

blocks.note: re means concerning, as in the heading of a letter
works is a word for a manufacturing plant
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A rebel sulks about working conditions at a plant, a Republican among the stubborn workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: The Republican letter sits just after the first letter of the works, and the word for about goes in front of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Refractory describes a person who stubbornly resists control or authority, a close synonym of defiant.

blocks.note: surface reading: a person laughs when someone tickles them
setter's reading: the phrase 'tickle someone's funny bone' has a sibling, parts of the chest that when tickled mean you are entertained

explanation.walkthrough: Having your sides or chest tickled is the idiom for being amused; the answer names the body parts that get tickled.
explanation.definitionFit: The bones of the chest are where a hearty laugh is felt, and to tickle them is an idiom for amusing someone.

clue.text: One enthusiastic about centre for business?

definitions.text: One enthusiastic about centre for business?

indicators.note: a centre is the heart of something, so only its innermost letters are kept
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: a fancier is an enthusiast, as in a pigeon fancier
the two central letters of the eight-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone keen on the heart of commerce, perhaps a City type, is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a person keen on money matters at the centre of the business world.
explanation.definitionFit: A financier manages large sums of money and investments, plausibly someone keen on the core of commerce.

clue.text: Open stove with pastry I dropped

blocks.note: an Aga is a British brand of cast-iron range cooker
a pie is a pastry dish
taken as written; this is the letter removed

explanation.surface: Instructions for a kitchen: open the oven, and you find the pastry has fallen.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a big British range cooker, a crossword favourite for stove.
explanation.definitionFit: Agape means wide open, used of a mouth gaping in wonder or surprise.

indicators.note: de-tailed means with the tail cut off, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: the definite article
inner thoughts are private or secret ones

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a secret turns out thin on detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detailed' seems to mean thorough, but read as de-tailed it strips the last letter from the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Both comparatives describe material that is less substantial or less robust than another.

clue.text: Leisure maybe includes stroll for stroller

indicators.note: to include is to hold within, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: R and R, rest and recreation, is an example of leisure
to amble is to walk at a leisurely pace

explanation.surface: A leisure activity is defined as going for a stroll if you are a walker.
explanation.walkthrough: R and R (rest and recreation) is the letter pair for leisure; the stroll goes between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A rambler is someone who walks in the countryside for pleasure, much as a stroller takes a leisurely walk.

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: the van is the front of an army or procession, as in vanguard
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Whoever walks at the front of the parade struts with self-importance.
explanation.walkthrough: Van as the leading part is short for vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A swaggering person shows off with conceit, and vain means excessively proud of oneself.

clue.text: Decrease of staff, say, in casualty?

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

blocks.note: a bat is a kind of stick or staff, hence 'say'
A and E, accident and emergency, is the British name for a hospital casualty department

explanation.surface: Hospital staffing numbers are falling in the casualty department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' reads as hospital personnel but is a stick; casualty is the British hospital emergency department, A and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen or diminish in force, a straightforward synonym for the verb decrease.

indicators.note: something tied round is bound up inside a wrapping, so the letters sit enclosed within the words

blocks.note: the run starts after the first letter of the opening word and ends with the first letter of the last

explanation.surface: A flask has been strapped around its base, perhaps for a picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: The brand name looks like the thing to manipulate, but the answer is simply sitting across the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: Nethermost means lowest or furthest down, so it describes the bottom position of anything.

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
an RA is a Royal Academician, a painter
a grant is an allowance of money

explanation.surface: A kind woman has handed an artist an allowance to live on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' seems to describe the woman's nature, but it defines the answer; RA (Royal Academician) is the usual crossword painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet can describe a pleasant smell, and fragrant means having a pleasing scent.

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so one piece is taken inside another

blocks.note: Bali is an island of Indonesia
Eng is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A holiday island in Indonesia takes up English as its language.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'English language' one phrase; the language wanted is a different one.
explanation.definitionFit: Bengali is the tongue spoken in Bangladesh and West Bengal in India.

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

a rant is an angry outburst
D is the abbreviation for Democrat

explanation.surface: A sharp-tongued Democrat launches into a second angry outburst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like an ordinal but means a short moment, MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant describes sharply sarcastic or biting wit, the same cutting quality as incisive remarks.

clue.text: Assume the French knight returned blessed

indicators.note: to return is to go back, so these letters run backwards

blocks.note: to infer is to conclude or presume
la is a French word for the
N is knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A French knight comes home and is taken to be holy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blessed' is used ironically, as in 'this blessed car won't start', which is the opposite of holy.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild ironic intensifiers for something irritating, as in that infernal noise or that blessed noise.

clue.text: Good land, even being ecclesiastical, initially

definitions.text: Good land, even being ecclesiastical, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives only its opening letter

blocks.note: first letters of the five words

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines the answer: a glebe is a piece of land belonging to a parish church, farmed to support the vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: Glebe is a plot of farmland assigned to a clergyman as part of his benefice, so church-owned ground.

clue.text: Nosed around, over cocky, having grounds?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so one piece goes about another

blocks.note: to nose about is to pry
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
pert means saucy or cheeky

explanation.surface: Someone snooped about, overconfident, as if they had a good reason to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having grounds' reads as having justification, but grounds here are land and estates.
explanation.definitionFit: Propertied describes people who own land or estates, so they literally possess grounds.

clue.text: Single included in list for party

indicators.note: being included in something means placed within it

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one, a single
a roster is a list of duties or names

explanation.surface: A lone name has been added to the guest list for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks like a noun but is the verb: to celebrate noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to revel boisterously, which is what you do when you party.

blocks.note: a tun is a large cask
G is the abbreviation for good
the Sten was a British submachine gun

explanation.surface: A gun barrel made of good quality metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrel' and 'gun' seem to belong together, but the barrel is a cask and the gun is separate; the Sten is a Second World War British weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: Tungsten is a hard, dense chemical element, a metal used in filaments and alloys.

clue.text: Pragmatism of Isles within British Isles?

indicators.note: within means inside, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: Is is the abbreviation for Isles, as on maps
the British Isles are, by example, a kingdom or realm

explanation.surface: A political writer discusses practical thinking in the islands inside the British Isles.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the British Isles are just one example of a realm.
explanation.definitionFit: Realism is the practical attitude of accepting things as they are, much like pragmatism.

clue.text: Raised in Basilicata, Roman Italian lover

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is sitting inside the following words
in a down clue, raised means lifted upward, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the region name, the whole of the middle word and the start of the last

explanation.surface: An Italian lover from Rome grew up in the southern region of Basilicata.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian lover' looks like the definition, but the last word contributes its first letter to the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: Inamorata is a borrowed Italian word for a woman who is loved, a female sweetheart.

clue.text: One perhaps separates acquiring new lover

indicators.note: to acquire is to take in, so one piece gains another inside it

blocks.note: one who parts things is a parter, a coined agent noun
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone splits from a partner and finds a new lover.
explanation.walkthrough: The agent noun is made up from the verb part, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A partner is the person you are in a romantic relationship with, so a lover.

clue.text: Fast fleet hasn’t run into sailors

indicators.note: not having something means it is missing, so a letter is taken away
going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: an armada is a fleet of warships
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: A quick naval fleet has failed to chase into the sailors' path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective for the fleet but is the noun meaning a period of not eating.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month during which Muslims abstain from food and drink from dawn to sunset.

clue.text: Crosses made from stake with beams

blocks.note: a stake is money wagered, a bet
beams of light are rays

explanation.surface: Wooden crosses are constructed from a post and some timber beams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crosses' pictures crucifixes built from stakes and beams; it is the verb, as in double-crosses.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross someone is to double-cross them, deceiving or being disloyal, which is to betray.

blocks.note: a bar is a pub
rage is extreme anger

explanation.surface: Tempers flare in a pub and it ends in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a plain pub brawl; the words simply join in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a concentrated artillery bombardment or a sustained attack, so an assault.

indicators.note: something worn is enclosed by what wears it

blocks.note: to sack a town is to plunder or rob it
the heart of sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A girlfriend puts on shapeless sacks instead of proper frocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweetheart' reads as darling, but it splits into sweet and its heart; 'sacks' is the verb meaning plunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Robes are long loose garments, and dresses is used here as a plural noun for such gowns.

indicators.note: a passenger aboard is carried inside, so one piece rides within another

blocks.note: a bus is a vehicle
St, saint, is a virtuous person

explanation.surface: A police officer nabs a good citizen riding on a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collars' could be shirt parts; here it is slang for arrests.
explanation.definitionFit: Both collar and bust are informal verbs for police arresting somebody.

indicators.note: snubbed suggests cut short, like a snub nose, so the end is lopped off

blocks.note: Jean-Paul Marat was a leader of the French Revolution
to hone is to perfect or refine

explanation.surface: A radical ignores a flawless competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snubbed' reads as ignored, but it truncates the verb for perfect; Marat is the standard crossword revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: A marathon is a long-distance running race, so it is one kind of competitive event.

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means raised upward, so the letters read bottom to top

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
loot is plunder or booty

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.definitionFit: A dose is a measured quantity of a drug swallowed at one time.

blocks.note: inst., instant, is old commercial shorthand for this month
ea is the abbreviation for each

explanation.surface: A schedule suggests doing something daily this month, ideally.
explanation.walkthrough: Inst (instant) appeared in old business letters, as in 'your letter of the 5th inst.', meaning the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead and preferably both express choosing one option in place of another alternative.

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
